sections.sectionSummaryBrief: This section explains that the revelation at Sinai was from the Essence of the light beyond revelation, yet it still involved order and gradation to bring about the ultimate delight of Atzmus with mankind.

translations.translation: And the explanation of this matter is,
behold,
the totality of the revelation that occurred at the time of the Giving of the Torah,
is not from the aspect of light that is within the category of revelation,
but rather from the aspect of the Essence of the light which is entirely above the category of revelation,
concealment in its very essence,
and even to the level of Atzmus,
"Anochi Mi She'Anochi" (I am that I am),
which is not hinted at by any letter nor by any crownlet.
And this does not contradict what was stated previously, that the revelation of the Giving of the Torah came after the preparation of the Exodus from Egypt and the Counting of the Omer,
because,
in addition to the fact that even in the aspect that is above the order of Hishtalshelus (the chain of descent),
and even in the aspect of the Essence of the light that is above the category of revelation,
there is order and gradation,
and as explained elsewhere,
the example for this is the matter of miracles,
that even though they are above the order of Hishtalshelus,
nevertheless, there is order and gradation within them,
behold, there is yet another point,
in order that the aspect of the essential delights (Sha'ashu'im HaAtzmiyim) be drawn down below, even to the aspect of "and My delights are with the children of man,"
it was necessary for there to be order and gradation in this.

sections.sectionSummaryBrief: This section discusses the two types of "voice" (Kla D'Ishtama and Kla D'La Ishtama) and how the revelation at Sinai was a "great voice that never ceases," drawn down through skipping and jumping, representing two modes of divine influx.

translations.translation: And this is what is written,
"The voice of my Beloved, behold He comes, skipping upon the mountains, leaping upon the hills."
"The voice of my Beloved" refers to the aspect of the voice that is not heard (Kla D'La Ishtama),
for behold, it is written,
"HaKal Kol" (the sound, a voice),
"Kal" is missing a Vav and "Kol" is full with a Vav,
these two aspects are the voice that is heard (Kla D'Ishtama) and the voice that is not heard (Kla D'La Ishtama).
The voice that is heard is the voice drawn from the intellect,
or from the emotions,
or from the intellect as it is revealed through the emotions.
And this voice is a voice that ceases (Kla D'Pasik),
for since its matter is the revelation of intellect and emotions, which are measured and limited,
therefore, when the matters that are drawn and revealed through it are concluded,
the voice also ceases automatically.
However, the voice that is not heard is a voice that is above intellect,
whose matter, in the service of man, is the cry of the heart that is above reason and knowledge,
and Above, it is the matter of drawing down the aspect of the Essence of the light, which in itself is above the category of revelation.
And this voice is a voice that does not cease (Kla D'La Pasik),
because limitation and cessation do not apply to it at all.
And this is what is written regarding the voice at the Giving of the Torah,
"A great voice, and it did not cease,"
for the revelation of the Giving of the Torah is the drawing down of the Essence which is above the category of revelation,
a voice that does not cease.
And furthermore,
since the voice itself is a voice that does not cease, to which cessation and change do not apply,
therefore, also the matters that were drawn down through it,
namely the Torah that was given with this voice,
change does not apply to it, Heaven forbid,
this being that the Torah will never be exchanged.
And behold,
even though this voice is a drawing down that is above the category of Hishtalshelus and above the category of revelation,
nevertheless, it is written "skipping... leaping,"
that skipping and leaping are with the legs,
because every drawing down is through the aspect of "leg,"
the lowest aspect.
And this means,
that this principle—that every drawing down is through the aspect of "leg"—
is not only regarding the drawings down within the order of Hishtalshelus,
where the inwardness of the upper becomes a surrounding light (Makif) for the lower,
and the Netzach-Hod-Yesod of the upper become intellect (Mochin) for the lower,
but rather it is also so regarding drawings down that are above Hishtalshelus.
And like the drawing down from the aspect of Atik,
which is only from the letter Tav,
and likewise the drawing down from the light that preceded the Tzimtzum,
which is only from the aspect of Malchus of Malchus,
and likewise regarding the coming of Moshiach it is written,
"And His feet shall stand."
And within this drawing down itself there are two aspects,
skipping and leaping,
as it states in the Mishnah,
"One skips with one foot and leaps with two feet."
And the difference between them is,
that when one skips with one foot,
behold, besides the fact that the body remains in its place and the entire drawing down is only in the aspect of the leg alone,
furthermore, even within the aspect of the leg itself, one foot is on the ground,
and what is drawn down is only one leg alone,
however, when one leaps with two feet,
behold, even though the drawing down is through the legs,
nevertheless,
behold, through his legs his entire body is moved,
meaning that he is drawn down in his entire essence.

sections.sectionSummaryBrief: This section explains the difference between skipping and leaping as two types of divine influx, corresponding to the near surrounding light (Makif HaKarov) and the distant surrounding light (Makif HaRachok), and how the near surrounding light causes contraction and concealment of the inner faculties.

translations.translation: And the explanation of the difference between the two matters of skipping and leaping
(even though both are a drawing down from above Hishtalshelus)
will be understood based on what is known, that also in the surrounding light (Makif) that is above Hishtalshelus there are two aspects,
the near surrounding light (Makif HaKarov) and the distant surrounding light (Makif HaRachok).
The near surrounding light is that which has a connection to the inner (Pnimi),
for although it is a surrounding light,
nevertheless, it has a connection to the inner,
and moreover,
in its concealment, the surrounding light encompasses the inner,
and afterward, when the inner is drawn from it,
the surrounding light guards over it.
However, the distant surrounding light has no connection to the inner at all.
And the explanation of their matter in the soul of man,
behold, our sages of blessed memory said,
"Five names are called for her: Nefesh, Ruach, Neshamah, Chayah, Yechidah."
Nefesh, Ruach, Neshamah are inner (Pnimi'im),
and Chayah and Yechidah are surrounding lights (Makifim),
except that Yechidah is the distant surrounding light,
and Chayah is the near surrounding light,
and this means,
that the surrounding light of Chayah is felt in the inner faculties.
And as it is written regarding Daniel, "And I, Daniel, alone saw the vision, and the men who were with me did not see the vision, but a great trembling fell upon them,"
and the Gemara asks,
"Since they did not see, why were they terrified?"
and it answers,
"Even though they themselves did not see, their Mazal saw,"
and this means,
that regarding Daniel this was in the aspect of inwardness,
in the aspect of sight,
as it is written "and I saw,"
but the men who were with me did not see the vision,
but nevertheless, the surrounding light was felt in them,
which is why a great trembling fell upon them.
And therefore the surrounding light is called "Mazal,"
from the term "Nozel" (flowing),
because from it flows and drips to the inner faculties.
And behold,
the effect that came from the feeling of the surrounding light was the matter of trembling,
for trembling removes the blood,
which is the matter of contraction and concealment,
and this means,
that from the revelation of the surrounding light, contraction and concealment occur in all the faculties.
And the explanation of the matter is,
that even in inner faculties we see that when a higher faculty is revealed,
then the lower faculty is in concealment.
And as with the faculties of Chochmah and Binah,
Chochmah is the matter of seeing the essence,
and when there is seeing of the essence,
then the matter of understanding and comprehension does not apply at all,
and only when the aspect of sight is concealed and only an intellectual premise remains
[And this means,
that because it is in the aspect of Chochmah,
this is not in a manner of understanding,
but rather in a manner of a premise,
and nevertheless, this is an intellectual premise,
which already belongs to the intellect],
then intellectual understanding is possible.
And it is found,
that the revelation of the faculty of Binah is specifically after the concealment of Chochmah,
but during the revelation of Chochmah,
Binah is in concealment.
And so it is also regarding the matter of the intellect (Mochin) and emotions (Midos),
that the revelation of the emotions is specifically after the intellect is concealed in the constriction of the throat.
And if in inner faculties it is so,
that when a higher faculty is revealed,
then the lower faculty is in concealment,
then certainly it is so regarding the revelation of the surrounding light,
that then all the inner faculties are in contraction and concealment.
And as with the faculty of will (Ratzon),
that when the will is revealed,
then it is impossible for there to be a revelation of the inner faculties,
like the revelation of the intellect.
And moreover,
even when the will is related to the intellect,
meaning that one wills to become wise,
nevertheless,
when the will shines with intensity,
it is impossible for there to be a revelation of the intellect at that time.
And this is that the effect produced from the fact that "their Mazal saw" is the matter of "a great trembling fell upon them,"
because,
Mazal is the surrounding light of Chayah,
and through the revelation of the surrounding light, all the inner faculties are concealed,
and therefore a trembling fell upon them,
for the matter of trembling, which removes the blood, is the concealment of all the faculties,
since life-force is clothed in the blood,
behold, through the removal of the blood, all the life-force is concealed.
And in more detail,
behold, the concealment that occurs through the removal of the blood is in all three aspects of Nefesh, Ruach, and Neshamah that are clothed in the body.
And the explanation of the matter is,
that in the human body there are three general organs,
as the statement,
"Three rulers are they: the brain, the heart, and the liver,"
in which are clothed the three aspects of Nefesh, Ruach, and Neshamah,
Neshamah in the brain,
Ruach in the heart,
and Nefesh in the liver.
And behold,
the clothing of the Nefesh is in the blood of the liver,
and it is obvious that through the removal of the blood, all the faculties belonging to the aspect of Nefesh are concealed.
And also the Ruach in the heart,
behold, the spirit in the right cavity
is connected with the spirit in the left cavity which is full of blood.
And also the Neshamah in the brain,
behold, we see that at the time of a fast, when there is a diminution of blood,
then one cannot understand and comprehend properly.
And all this is regarding the aspect of the near surrounding light,
which is felt in the inner faculties,
however, the distant surrounding light,
the surrounding light of Yechidah,
is distant from the inner faculties and is not felt in them.
